Delhi Police argues reel‑makers not covered by journalist protection in Supreme Court

Delhi Police submitted an affidavit to the Supreme Court asserting that social media influencers, content creators and reel‑makers do not qualify as journalists and therefore are not entitled to the press‑protective provisions that apply to journalists covering protests, emphasizing that the court’s direction applies only to bona‑fide journalists. Independent reporters who covered the anti‑SIR protests criticised the police position, saying it dismisses ground reportage, undermines digital journalism and overlooks their work. No court ruling on the matter has been reported yet.
